newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nafin auctions 1.5 bln pesos in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nafin auctions 1.5 bln pesos in bonds.

text.p: Mexican development bank Nacional Financiera (Nafin) on Wednesday said it had auctioned 1.5 billion pesos of bank development bonds.
The bonds, called NAFTIIE, with maturities of 18 months and 36 months, were auctioned on Tuesday, it said in a statement.
Nafin said the bonds, which are to be issued on Thursday, were placed "with the objective of granting long-term credits at variable rates."
Despite unfavourable conditions related to volatility in emerging markets, the bank was able to place the paper at "excellent" rates, it said.
It said the 18-month paper was placed at TIIE minus 0.78 percent and at TIIE minus 0.52 percent for the three year paper. The TIIE is a market-weighted average interbank rate.
Nafin said demand for the 18-month paper was 6.6 times the amount offered. Demand for the three-year bond was 3.4 times the amount offered.
The 36-month paper will be placed at an amount of 1.0 bilion pesos, while the 18-month paper will be for 500 million pesos, it said
